purpose: Labetalol is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain from serious damage. It can be used alone or along with other blood pressure medicines.
how_it_works: Your heart and blood vessels have special receptors that control how hard your heart pumps and how tight your blood vessels are. Labetalol works by blocking two types of these receptors — alpha and beta — at the same time. This causes your heart to beat a little slower and with less force, and it helps your blood vessels relax and widen, which lowers your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: Feeling dizzy or lightheaded, especially when you stand up quickly. Tiredness or fatigue. Headache, upset stomach, or nausea. Tingling of the scalp or skin. Stuffy nose. These effects are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts.
warnings: Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first — stopping abruptly can cause serious heart problems. Tell your doctor if you have asthma, breathing problems, diabetes, or liver disease, as labetalol may not be right for you or may need close monitoring. It can mask some signs of low blood sugar if you are diabetic. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual starting dose is 100 mg taken by mouth twice a day (morning and evening). Your doctor may gradually increase your dose over time, up to a maximum of 2,400 mg per day in divided doses, depending on how your blood pressure responds. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, with or without food.
